quickstart.question: I'm new. Where should I start?
quickstart.a1: Start in [Generate concept mockups] by writing the mood in one sentence. Different concepts appear as a gallery. It does not build a full site.
quickstart.a2: When generation finishes, several concepts appear. Lock one you like, then refine tokens and add mockups of other scenes.
quickstart.a3: Before lock you only compare concepts. After lock, work continues on that one concept.

requirements-writing.question: How should I write the brief for better results?
requirements-writing.a1: Say who uses the service and what mood, color, and type you want. Visual cues like 'navy and gold, large type, generous whitespace, trustworthy' work better than 'make it clean'.
requirements-writing.a2: Attach references if you have them. Briefs, requirement docs, and existing screenshots have their text extracted and used with the brief.
requirements-writing.a3: Input is auto-saved every 30 seconds, so you can leave and continue later.

concept-vs-variant.question: What is the difference between a concept and a mockup?
concept-vs-variant.a1: A concept is **a design-system direction**. One token set — color, type, radius, shadow — is one concept.
concept-vs-variant.a2: A mockup is **another arrangement of the same scene's concept board**. It is not a finished site page. It is a direction mockup of a hero scene such as main (key visual, palette, type).
concept-vs-variant.a3: So '3 concepts × 5 mockups' is not 15 different web pages. It is 5 mockups of the same scene for each of 3 directions.

add-screen.question: I also want other scenes (main, login, and more).
add-screen.a1: After locking a concept, use [Add scene] on the workspace. It keeps the locked design system and only pulls concept mockups of the new scene.
add-screen.a2: Increasing the mockup count does not produce another scene. Mockups are variants of the same scene.
add-screen.a3: Add scene does not rebuild tokens, so it is faster than the first generation and sits on the same system.

concept-lock.question: I locked a concept but want a different one.
concept-lock.a1: Unlock on the workspace to compare every concept again.
concept-lock.a2: Screens added and token edits stay bound to the locked concept. They do not follow if you switch.

generation-warning.question: The result has a 'warning' mark.
generation-warning.a1: A step did not come back in the expected format, so a fallback style was used. The screen still renders, but it may differ from the intended result.
generation-warning.a2: In this case **one retry does not count against usage.** If you dislike the result, generate again.

concurrent-generation.question: I see 'A generation is already in progress'.
concurrent-generation.a1: Only one generation can run per account. If another project is generating, wait until it finishes.
concurrent-generation.a2: You can cancel the in-progress generation from that project.

ds-mode.question: What is 'Unified DS'?
ds-mode.a1: Instead of a fully separate system per concept, base tokens (type, spacing, radius) stay shared and only accent color families change.
ds-mode.a2: It fits when you already have brand rules and only want to compare color. Available on Pro and above.

token-edit.question: Can I edit tokens myself?
token-edit.a1: Edit them in the right-hand workspace panel. Changes apply to the mockup preview immediately.
token-edit.a2: The editable range depends on the plan. Free can edit color families; Pro and above can also adjust typography, spacing, radius, and shadow.
token-edit.a3: If you change something by mistake, use Ctrl/Cmd+Z.

export-formats.question: Which formats can I export?
export-formats.a1: PNG is available on every plan. Free PNG includes a watermark.
export-formats.a2: Token JSON (W3C DTCG), CSS variables, and Figma files are available on Pro and above.
export-formats.a3: Export history is kept per project so you can download again.

mcp.question: I want to use tokens directly in Cursor or Claude Code.
mcp.a1: Issue a key in [Settings → API Key], then connect the repo MCP server to your coding tool. It reads locked tokens, screen structure, and component styles.
mcp.a2: You do not copy values by hand. After you edit tokens, the next call receives the new values.
mcp.a3: This path is read-only. A leaked key cannot change the project.

plan-limits.question: How do plans differ?
plan-limits.a1: Free includes 3 generations / month, 1 concept × 3 mockups, and PNG export with a watermark.
plan-limits.a2: Pro includes 30 generations / month, 3 concepts × 3 or 5 mockups, Unified DS, all Export formats, and API Key.
plan-limits.a3: Team has no generation cap and adds team seats and sharing.

credits.question: I used up this month's generations.
credits.a1: Buy extra credits to generate beyond the monthly cap. Credits are deducted as you use them.
credits.a2: The cap resets every month. Check remaining uses in [Usage].

account-locked.question: My login is locked.
account-locked.a1: Five failed password attempts lock the account for 15 minutes. This blocks credential stuffing.
account-locked.a2: It unlocks automatically after 15 minutes. If you need it sooner, ask an administrator.

two-factor.question: I want two-factor authentication.
two-factor.a1: Register an authenticator app (Authy, Google Authenticator, and others) in [Settings → Security]. Login then also asks for a 6-digit code.
two-factor.a2: Store the backup codes shown at setup. If you lose the device, those codes are the only recovery path.

delete-account.question: I want to delete my account and data.
delete-account.a1: Request deletion in [Settings → Security]. Access stops immediately, and data is permanently deleted after the grace period.
delete-account.a2: You can download your data first. It includes projects, tokens, and generation history.
